questions.q:
In a cell, the following reactions take place

${Fe}^{2 +} \to {Fe}^{3 +} + e^{-}E^{o}{Fe}^{3 +} / {Fe}^{2 +} = 0 . 77V$

$2I^{-} \to {I}_{2} + 2e^{-}{E}_{{I}_{2} / I^{-}}^{0} = 0 . 54V$

The standard electrode potential for the spontaneous reaction in the cell is $x \times {10}^{- 2}Vat298K$. The value of~$x$ is - (Nearest Integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The electrode which has more reduction potential will get reduced in spontaneous reaction in the cell. So, spontaneous reaction will be&

$2{Fe}^{3 +}\left(aq\right) + 2I^{-}\left(aq\right) \to 2{Fe}^{2 +}\left(aq\right) + {I}_{2}$

Iron will act as cathode and Iodine will act as anode.

$E^{0}cell = \left(E^{0}RP\right)C - \left(E^{0}RP\right)A$

$= 0 . 77 - 0 . 54$

$= 0 . 23V$

$= 23 \times {10}^{- 2}V$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Charge& \left(q\right) = it = 2 \times 8 \times 60 = 960C$

$\dfrac{960}{96000} = 0 . 01F$

${Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -} + 14H^{+} + 6e^{-} \to 2{Cr}^{3 +} + 7{H}_{2}O$

$0 . 01F\dfrac{1}{3} \times 0 . 01mole$

Theoritical mass of~${Cr}^{3 +} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{600}{96000} \times 52 = 0 . 173g$

So, efficiency~$= \dfrac{Wactual}{WTheoritial} \times 100 = \dfrac{0 . 104}{0 . 173} \times 100 = 60 %$

The logarithm of equilibrium constant for the reaction ${Pd}^{2 +} + 4{Cl}^{-} ⇌ {PdCl}_{4}^{2 -}$ is
(Nearest integer)

Given: $\dfrac{2 . 303RT}{F} = 0 . 06V$

${Pd}_{( aq )}^{2 +} + 2e^{-} ⇌ Pd ( s ) E^{o} = 0 . 83V$

${PdCl}_{4}^{2 -} ( aq ) + 2e^{-} ⇌ Pd ( s ) + 4{Cl}^{-} ( aq )$

$E^{o} = 0 . 65V$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given,& $\dfrac{2 . 303RT}{F} = 0 . 06V$

Using gibbs free energy equation,

$\Delta G ° = - RTlnK$

$- {nFE}_{cell }^{o} = - RT \times 2 . 303 \left(\log_{10}K\right)$

${E}_{Cell}^{0}0 . 06 \timesn = logK - - - - - - - - - ( i )$

${Pd}^{2 +} ( aq ) + 2e^{-} ⇌ Pd ( s ) , {E}_{cathode, reduction }^{0} = 0 . 83V$

$Pd ( s ) + 4{Cl}^{-} ( aq . ) ⇌ {PdCl}_{4}^{2 -} ( aq ) + 2e^{-}, {E}_{anode, oxidation}^{o} = 0 . 65V$

Net Reaction~$\to {Pd}^{2 +} ( aq . ) + 4{Cl}^{-} ( aq . ) ⇌ {PdCl4}^{2 -} ( aq . )$

${E}_{cell }^{o} = {E}_{cathode,reduction}^{o} - {E}_{anode, oxidation }^{o}$

$⇒ {E}_{cell}^{o} = 0 . 83 - 0 . 65 ⇒ {E}_{cell}^{o} = 0 . 18 - - - - - - - - ( ii )$

Also $n = 2 - - - - - - - - ( iii )$

Using equation $( i ) , ( ii )$& $( iii )$, we get

${E}_{Cell}^{0}0 . 06 \timesn = logK$

$⇒ $\dfrac{0 . 18}{0 . 06} \times$2 = logK$

$⇒ logK = 6

$

questions.q: Resistance of a conductivity cell (cell constant $129m^{- 1}$) filled with $74 . 5ppm$ solution of $KCl$ is $100Ω$ (labelled as solution $1$). When the same cell is filled with $KCl$ solution of $149$ ppm, the resistance is $50Ω$ (labelled as solution $2$). The ratio of molar conductivity of solution~$1$ and solution $2$~is i.e. $\dfrac{∧ 1}{∧ 2} = x \times {10}^{- 3}$. The value of $x$~is____Given, molar mass of $KCl$ is~$74 . 5g{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given& $\dfrac{l}{A} = 129m^{- 1}$

$KCl$ solution $1$:

$74 . 5ppm, {R}_{1} = 100Ω$

$KCl$ solution $2$:

$149ppm, {R}_{2} = 50Ω$

Here,~$\dfrac{ppm1}{ppm2} = \dfrac{M1}{M2}$

and~$κ = \dfrac{1}{R}G * whereG * = cellconstant$

Since value of cell constant is same in both the cases.

$\dfrac{k1}{k2} = \dfrac{R2}{R1}$

$\dfrac{∧ 1}{∧ 2} = \dfrac{{k}_{1} \times \dfrac{1000}{M1}}{{k}_{2} \times \dfrac{1000}{M2}}$

$= \dfrac{K1}{{K}_{2}} \times \dfrac{M2}{M1} = \dfrac{R2}{{R}_{1}} \times \dfrac{M2}{M1}$

$= \dfrac{50}{100} \times \dfrac{149}{74 . 5} = 1$

$= \dfrac{∧ 1}{∧ 2} = 1, 000 \times {10}^{- 3}$

questions.q: Electrolysis of 600 mL aqueous solution of NaCl for 5 min changes the pH of the solution to 12 . The current in Amperes used for the given electrolysis is ____. (Nearest integer).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Electrolysis of NaCl is
$\mathrm{NaCl}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \mathrm{NaOH}(\mathrm{aq})+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{~g})+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g})$ Since during electrolysis pH changes to 12
So \left[\mathrm{OH}^{\ominus}\right]=10^{-2}$ and \left[\mathrmH^{+}\right]=10^{-12}$
So by Faraday law
Gram amount of substance deposited = Amount of electricity passed $\begin{aligned} & 10^{-2} \times \frac{600}{1000} \times 96500=\mathrm{I} \times \mathrm{t} \\ & \frac{10^{-2} \times 600}{1000} \times 96500=\mathrm{I} \times 5 \times 60 \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{10^{-2} \times 600 \times 96500}{1000 \times 5 \times 60} \\ & \mathrm{I}=1.93 \text { ampere } \\ & \text { So }, I=2 \text { ampere (nearest integer) }\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A $KCl$ solution of conductivity $0 . 14Sm^{- 1}$ shows a resistance of $4 . 19Ω$ in a conductivity cell. If the same cell is filled with an $HCl$~solution, the resistance drops to $1 . 03Ω$. The conductivity of the HCl solution is ____\times {10}^{- 2}Sm^{- 1}. (Round off to the Nearest Integer).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The thermal conductivity of a material is a measure of its ability to conduct heat. It is commonly denoted by $κ$, \lambda, or \kappa. Heat transfer occurs at a lower rate in materials of low thermal conductivity than in materials of high thermal conductivity

$κ = \dfrac{1}{R} \cdot G^{*}$

For same conductivity cell, $G^{*}$ is constant and hence $κ \cdot R . =$ constant.

$∴ 0 . 14 \times 4 . 19 = κ \times 1 . 03$

or, $= \dfrac{0 . 14 \times 4 . 19}{1 . 03}$

$= 0 . 5695{Sm}^{- 1}$

$= 56 . 95 \times {10}^{- 2}{Sm}^{- 1} \approx 57 \times {10}^{- 2}{Sm}^{- 1}$

questions.q: The resistivity of a $0 . 8M$~solution of an electrolyte is $5 \times {10}^{- 3}Ωcm$. Its molar conductivity is ${10}^{4}{Ω}^{- 1}{cm}^{2}{mol}^{- 1}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given,
Resistivity $( ρ ) = 5 \times {10}^{- 3}Ωcm$

Molarity $( M ) = 0 . 8M$

Thus, Molar conductivity of electrolyte~\left({λ}_{M}\right) = \dfrac{1}{ρ} \times \dfrac{1000}{M}$

$= \dfrac{1}{5 \times {10}^{- 3}} \times \dfrac{1000}{0 . 8}$

$= 0 . 25 \times {10}^{6}$

$= 25 \times {10}^{4}{cm}^{2}{mol}^{- 1}$.

$
